column1: # One row per wordlist, tab separated:
# tier  ship   The file is committed. A fresh clone has it, so every capability
#               that needs it runs with no setup and no operator input.
# tier  fetch  The file is too large for a git repository: GitHub and Codeberg
#               both refuse blobs over 100 MB. Run ./fetch-wordlists.sh once.
#               These rows always carry a pinned SHA-256.
# The path is relative to wordlists/, which is also the root the capability
# catalog resolves `{wl:...}` references against. A reference names a path
# `{wl:ssh/passwords.txt}` are both valid and mean different things: the first
# is the general password corpus, the second the SSH-flavoured one. There is no
# single list standing in for every attack.
# `<sha256>` is `-` for ship rows; their digests are recorded in
# MANIFEST.sha256 by tools.sh and checked by ./verify-wordlists.sh.
